extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NEH grant applicants and potential panelists (scholars and humanities experts)
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the National Endowment for the Humanities' multi-level review process for grant applications, including panel review, staff synthesis, National Council deliberation, and the Chair's final decision. Also explains evaluator selection, conflicts of interest, ratings, and confidentiality/transparency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core NEH review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s review criteria emphasize humanities significance, the applicant’s abilities and qualifications, the proposal’s clarity of expression, and the project’s feasibility, design, cost, and work plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reviews and ratings must be based on NEH's published review criteria and program guidelines. Since review criteria may vary from program to program, applicants should consult the criteria of the grant program to which they are applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating scale for evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators may choose from the following ratings: E for Excellent, VG for Very Good, G for Good, SM for Some Merit, and NC for Not Competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators enter preliminary ratings online several weeks before the panel meeting and may raise or lower initial ratings after panel discussion; they provide individual ratings and are not expected to reach a panel consensus or rank applications as a panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluator selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers select evaluators for their expertise in the relevant disciplines, topics, and areas, as well as their overall breadth of knowledge in the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other considerations may include the type of institution the evaluator represents, their past panel experience, or other demographic characteristics. NEH recruits panelists from every state and forms panels anew for each competition (no standing panels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest and recusal
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases of a conflict of interest, evaluators will recuse themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recusal ensures reviews remain impartial; all remaining reviews and ratings must adhere to NEH's published review criteria and program guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review procedures (pre-meeting work and discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH provides evaluators with online access to applications several weeks in advance so they can read applications, enter preliminary comments, and assign initial ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some programs evaluators meet (in person or virtually) to discuss applications, enter additional written comments, and assign final ratings; program officers organize proceedings according to initial ratings and evaluators may change ratings informed by panel discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer eligibility checks and assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH program officers check applications for eligibility and assign them to panels based on academic discipline, institutional type, project area, or project type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically 15 to 40 applications are assigned to a panel and program officers select three to five evaluators per panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelist service limits
rubrics_metrics.description: No evaluator may serve in consecutive years for the same grant program or on more than two convening panels in any calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH does not maintain standing panels; all panels are formed anew at the start of a grant competition to diversify participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff synthesis and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: After panels complete their work, NEH staff organizes the panel results, and for each of the highest-rated applications summarizes the evaluators' reviews and comments and notes matters of fact or other significant issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on reviewers' ratings and comments, NEH staff recommends the most meritorious applications while maintaining an even level of quality among recommended proposals across all panels in a grant program. The recommended slate and supporting materials are made available to the National Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Council review and voting
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Council on the Humanities (an advisory body) meets twice a year to review staff recommendations; council members serve on committees that review recommendations, discuss individual applications, and vote on the staff’s recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a plenary session council members finalize their recommendations to the Chair. By law the Council is required to review applications for financial support before the Chair acts (with narrow statutory exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair's final funding decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The NEH Chair considers the totality of advice provided by reviewers, NEH staff, and the National Council and, by law, makes all final funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All levels of review prior to the Chair's decision are advisory; the Chair takes into account the advice but has statutory authority to make the final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and confidentiality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH seeks to be transparent while protecting confidentiality: it is public information that an evaluator served on a panel (announced in the Federal Register and annual reports), but panel meetings and Council sessions where applications are evaluated are not open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH announces award winners but does not announce unfunded applicants. Applicants may request evaluators' ratings and written comments; NEH does not provide the names of evaluators with their comments. Confidentiality commitments may be affected in FOIA litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedures and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants use NEH guidelines and the Grants.gov package to prepare materials and must submit the application package to Grants.gov by the program deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow program-specific application instructions and eligibility requirements; timely submission via Grants.gov is required.
